_about: The rifle set. barrelIn is the barrel length the loads' speeds are given for. sightHeightIn is how far the sight line sits above the bore for each sight the rifle can carry. boreOffsetMoa is the rifle's mechanical offset with the sight at its middle setting: the reason a sight needs zeroing. sights lists the sights (data/sights.json) the rifle can carry; defaultSight is the sight the rifle opened with before every sight could be chosen (the Vepr its scope, the others their iron sights), which an address without a sight still opens and whose old saved zero and shot log are read forward. firstCourse is the course the rifle opens on the first time on a device (then the last used). sightLeaf names, per iron sight that has more than one leaf table, which table this rifle's leaf follows (the 5.45x39 rifle's leaf is cut for its own load); a sight not named uses its own "leaf". range-day-thirteen: scopeMount is how a scope is mounted on the rifle: the kind of rail (rail: "picatinny" takes every mount of the scope collection; "rimfire-dovetail" takes none of them), in words, and the rail top's height over the bore (railHeightOverBoreIn); a collection scope's height over the bore on the rifle is that height plus its mount's (data/sights.json, mount.centerOverRailIn), worked out and checked by lib/guns.js. range-day-eighteen: scopeMount.ownScope is a rifle's own scope that is not one of the collection (the .22's Primary Arms CLx): the sight it names, the rings it sits in, the rings' saddle height over the dovetail and the receiver top's height over the bore; the scope's sightHeightIn is the saddle plus half its tube (data/sights.json, tubeMm) plus the receiver top, which test/data.test.js works out again.

fab-flipup.estimate: not published by FAB or IWI. The FAB pair stands at AR co-witness height ("same height as standard AR-15 sights", https://thetruthaboutguns.com/gear-review-fab-defense-fbs-rbs-iron-sights, search text), about 1.4 in over the rail; the Tavor's top rail sits about 2.25 in over the bore (the basis of the red dot's figure in this entry: a SAR owner measured 3.75 in with a scope in an AR-height mount). 2.25 + 1.4 = 3.65 in. (An X95 review puts an optic 1.1 in higher over the bore than on an AR, 3.7 against 2.6 in, https://smallarmsreview.com/?p=43528, search text: the same band.)

pa-md25.estimate: IWI publishes no rail height. Band from the sources: a Tavor SAR owner measured 3.75 in over the bore with a scope in an AR-height (about 1.5 in) mount (https://www.ar15.com/forums/armory/Tavor_sight_height_over_bore_/43-412550/), which puts the Tavor rail about 2.25 in over the bore; Manticore sells its rail as raising the factory rail about 1/2 in to AR height (https://manticorearms.com/product/x95-overwatch-full-length-top-rail/); an X95 owner puts its rail about 0.2 in under an AR's (https://www.ar15.com/forums/armory/Got-a-Tavor-X95--have-questions-on-optic-height-/43-472463/). The MD-25 ships with a low base (0.96 in to the dot's center) and a riser with spacers (1.41, 1.535 and 1.64 in) (https://www.optics-trade.eu/blog/primary-arms-slx-md-25-red-dot-sight-instruction-manual/, https://www.targettamers.com/red-dot-sights/primary-arms-slx-md-25-gen-ii-review/). So the dot sits between about 3.2 in (low base) and 3.9 in (riser and thick spacer) over the bore, the owner-reported band being 2.1 to 3.75. Within that band the engine puts the second crossing of a 50-yard zero with IMI M193 (3,066 fps) at 258 yd for 3.21 in, 290 yd for 3.75 in and 299 yd for 3.89 in; the brief's remembered zero was on at 50 and again near 300, so 3.89 in (the riser with its thick spacer) is used

seeall-gen1.estimate: not published by the maker. A reviewer measured the first SeeAll about 0.75 in tall above the rail (https://www.edcgeeks.com/review-seeall-opensight-mk1-rail-sight/, search text); the reticle's line on the block's top edge is taken 0.6 in over the rail; the Tavor's top rail sits about 2.25 in over the bore (as for the red dot): 2.85 in

barrelIn.estimate: the importer (FIME Group, https://fimegroup.com/vepr-rifle/vepr-762x54r/) lists the thumbhole-stock Vepr in 7.62x54R with 16.5 in (VPR-76254-01), 20.5 in (VPR-76254-02) and 23.2 in (VPR-76254-03) barrels; the brief describes a long barrel of about 18 in, so the 20.5-inch model is the nearest listed length and is used. If the rifle was the 23.2-inch model the loads' speeds rise by about 55 fps

vepr-irons.estimate: not published by Molot or FIME; AK-pattern irons sit 1.9 in over the bore (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AK-47), and one review of the .308 Vepr says about 4 in, which does not fit an AK receiver; 2.0 used

utg-bugbuster-3-9x32.estimate: no maker figure: the BugBuster sits on the Vepr's side-rail mount, about an inch above the irons (2.0 in), as the 2-7x44 was modeled before it (3.0 in); the mount, not the scope, sets the height, and the BugBuster's 32 mm front lens needs no taller rings than a 44 mm one, so 3.0 in is kept

up.estimate: a freshly mounted scope on a side rail is usually several minutes off; chosen so the rifle needs zeroing, not measured

right.estimate: same basis: the same basis as the figure next to it in this entry

recoilFactor.estimate: a 7.62x54R rifle kicks far harder than a 5.56 carbine; the brief asks for a longer recoil on this rifle

railHeightOverBoreIn.estimate: No maker figure for a side mount's rail over the bore could be read. A side mount is made to stand its rail clear over the receiver cover and the rear sight, so its top is taken level with the Vepr's own iron sight line, 2 in over the bore (the figure its irons use in this file); the prism sight already modeled on this kind of mount sits at 3.0 in, the same band once a mount's own height is added. The Vepr's rail is the AK pattern's: "almost any AK optic will fit" (https://russianoptics.net/Concepts.html, search text).

pa-clx-1-6x24.estimate: the scope's center over the bore in the Warne 731M rings (scopeMount.ownScope): the rings' saddle stands 0.4 in over the dovetail (a sourced figure), the 30 mm tube's center 0.591 in over the saddle (half the maker's 30 mm), and the receiver's top, where the dovetail is cut, 0.5 in over the bore (an estimate, scopeMount.ownScope.receiverTopOverBoreIn): 0.4 + 0.591 + 0.5 = 1.491 in

scopeMount.words: a receiver grooved for 3/8-inch tip-off rimfire mounts (Remington's open-sighted bolt-action .22s, e.g. the Model Five: "the receiver is grooved for tip-off scope mounts", https://www.gunblast.com/Remington-ModelFive.htm, search text). Its own scope, the Primary Arms CLx 1-6x24 (range-day-eighteen), sits in dovetail rings (ownScope). None of the scope collection's mounts clamps a dovetail, and an adapter rail is no part of this set, so the .22 offers none of the collection.

ownScope.rings: Warne 731M rimfire rings, 30 mm, medium, matte: steel rings that clamp a 3/8-inch (or 11 mm) dovetail and hold a 30 mm tube, the CLx's tube

source.note: the maker's page for the 731M: dimension B (the saddle's height, from the top of the dovetail to the bottom of the scope's tube) 0.400 in; retailers list the same ".400 in" saddle height (https://www.opticsplanet.com/warne-22-30mm-riflescope-rings.html). receiverTopOverBoreIn.estimate: no maker figure, and the rifle's model is not identified (barrelIn). Remington's bolt-action rimfires have a round receiver about an inch across with the bore on its axis, the dovetail grooves cut along its top, so the top stands about half an inch over the bore
